name: message-test-001-exp001-prescreen
question: How likely would you be to actually sign up and pay for this? Answer honestly as yourself, including any hesitations.

concepts.headline: Know your heart risk. Then actually lower it.
concepts.pitch: A board-certified physician tracks your ApoB, blood pressure, and coronary calcium score — and works with you to bring them down. Video visits and direct messaging. No insurance needed.

concepts.headline: Heart disease runs in your family. It doesn't have to run in you.
concepts.pitch: If a parent or sibling had a heart attack, your risk is real — and manageable. A board-certified physician baselines your numbers and manages them down with you, by video and text.

concepts.headline: Serious heart prevention. No insurance games.
concepts.pitch: No copays, no claims, no 15-minute rushed visits. One flat price for a physician who actually tracks your heart numbers and answers your messages.

concepts.headline: Your weight-loss program ended. Your health gains don't have to.
concepts.pitch: Research shows blood pressure and cholesterol improvements fade within 1-2 years of stopping. A board-certified physician tracks your numbers and protects the progress you paid for.

personas.description: 52-year-old male engineering manager in Troy, Michigan. Household income $145k, employer PPO insurance with high deductible. Just got a coronary calcium score of 280 from a $75 hospital screening promotion; his PCP said 'we'll keep an eye on it' and offered a statin with no follow-up plan. Analytical, reads studies, frustrated by 12-minute appointments. Has an HSA with $9k in it.

44-year-old female elementary school teacher in Grand Rapids, Michigan. Household income $98k, decent insurance through the district. Her father died of a heart attack at 58 and her older brother just got a stent at 49. She is scared but busy, skeptical of anything that feels like a wellness fad, and watches spending carefully.

38-year-old female HR coordinator in Warren, Michigan. Income $72k. Lost 48 pounds on compounded semaglutide from a telehealth company that just sent her a transition notice; branded versions cost $349/month which she cannot afford. Worried about regaining weight and her blood pressure creeping back up. Already used to paying ~$200/month for the old program.

41-year-old male self-employed flooring contractor in Lansing, Michigan. Income varies $60-90k, no health insurance, hasn't seen a doctor in 6 years. Smokes occasionally, knows his blood pressure was high at a pharmacy machine. Price-sensitive, distrusts the medical system, but his wife is pushing him to get checked.

35-year-old male software developer in Ann Arbor, Michigan. Income $165k, excellent insurance, listens to longevity podcasts, already pays $365/year for a Function Health membership and wears a Whoop. Wants ApoB optimization and someone qualified to interpret his data; allergic to anything that feels dumbed-down.

58-year-old female retail worker in Flint, Michigan. Household income $52k, insured through Marketplace bronze plan with $7k deductible. On lisinopril from an urgent care visit, no regular doctor. $99/month feels like a lot; she'd need to be convinced it replaces costs she's already paying.
